newsitem.title: INDIA: India tightens liquidity norms for finance firms.
newsitem.headline: India tightens liquidity norms for finance firms.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said it increased the percentage of liquid assets to be maintained by non-bank finance companies (NBFCs).

NBFCs now maintaining 5.0 percent of their deposits in government securities/guaranteed bonds should maintain 7.5 percent and 10 percent of the deposits in these securities from January 1 and April 1, 1998 respectively, it said in a press release issued late on Wednesday.

Other NBFCs now required to maintain 10 percent of their deposits in these assets will be required to maintain higher liquidity at 12.5 percent and 15 percent with effect from January 1 and April 1, 1998 respectively, RBI said.
There will be no change in the liquid assets requirement of 10 percent for the residuary non-bank firms.
RBI said the government securities/guaranteed bonds should be kept in the custody of one of the scheduled commercial banks located at the place where the NBFC has its registered office.

"These securities can be withdrawn by the NBFCs only for repayment to the depositors or for substitution of these securities with matching value or in the case of a reduction in the deposit in the deposit liabilities," RBI said.
